reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5, curriculum and design work delegated by George
factChecks: Independently recomputed all 118 numeric keys from their problem statements in packages/curriculum/tests/economics-content.test.ts: 58 lesson answers, 24 recall answers and 36 course-check answers. The test derives equilibria, surpluses, tax incidence, deadweight losses, midpoint elasticities, cost minima, monopoly outcomes and game totals from first principles, not from the activity engine.

Activity-engine tests check the closed-form surplus and deadweight-loss areas against numerical integrals of the curves, check that MC meets ATC at its minimum, and check best responses, Nash equilibria and repeated-game totals on prisoner's-dilemma and coordination games.

Reviewed all 48 teaching beats and 98 bounded explorer cases for units, sign conventions and stated assumptions (linear curves, per-unit taxes collected from sellers, constant marginal external cost and constant monopoly marginal cost). Models carry givens only; results appear only after an answer.

Fourteen lesson questions are selections or one-word answers; 8 of 72 lesson questions (11%) are multiple choice. One-word answers (Ben, sunk, right, Pigou, low, dilemma) were checked against the shipped text matcher with alternatives and rejected ideas.

Checked standard definitions and relationships against nineteen exact sections of OpenStax Principles of Microeconomics 3e (Greenlaw, Shapiro and MacDonald, 2022). The live web edition is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and its footer asks that the book not be ingested into large language models, so it is recorded as reference only. Section URLs were confirmed by HTTP status; two pages were opened only to confirm the licence and citation. All prose, numbers, problems, drawings and the cover are original.
Pigou's corrective tax is dated to The Economics of Welfare (1920) and his succession to Marshall's Cambridge chair from general knowledge, not from an inspected primary source.

Started a disposable local stack with the mock tutor and inspected the roadmap, every lesson's first explorer, later beats (externality, quota, repeated game), answered states and a placement item at 1440x900 and 390x844. Repaired overlapping labels, uneven axis ticks, an off-chart price probe and theme text colours.

Editorial review is by the authoring agent under delegated authority. There has been no independent human subject review or documented learner trial, and the browser suite in apps/web/e2e/economics-course.spec.ts has been written but not yet run.
changes: Added a twelve-lesson course in four modules (choice and cost, markets, welfare and policy, firms and strategy) with 72 questions, 24 recall cards and 48 answered visual beats.
Added twelve-item placement, mixed checkpoint and seven-day delayed transfer checks.

Added nine bounded economics explorer models (frontier, trade, margin, market, elasticity, costs, monopoly, payoff matrix, repeated game) with animated case changes, keyboard controls, finite playback and reduced motion.
